key_insight: Cova-PINN improves multi-domain PINN accuracy for fluid-solid conjugate heat transfer by enforcing conservation across thermal interaction paths instead of only within separately sampled domains.
engineering_relevance: This makes PINN predictions more reliable for heat-exchanger design, where correct outlet temperature and device-level energy balance matter as much as local field accuracy.
method: Cross-domain composite control-volume balances are optimized at the local scale.
Paired-wall closure is enforced at the full heat-exchanger scale.
Designed for complex geometries and evaluated on TPMS and DualMS CHT cases.
evidence_signal: Across four TPMS heat exchangers, Cova-PINN reduced average outlet-temperature error by 37.7% and device-level closure error by 60.2% relative to the closest baseline (MUSA-PINN-CHT), with consistent gains on DualMS.
watch_item: The framework adds coupled conservation constraints that may increase training complexity and sensitivity to how control volumes, interfaces, and sampling are defined.
paper_title: Cova-PINN: Cross-Domain Conservation Physics-Informed Neural Network for Fluid-Solid Conjugate Heat Transfer in Complex Geometries
